name: Why are my pipes making a hammering noise?

mainEntity.name: Why are my pipes making a hammering noise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hammering noises, often called 'water hammer,' occur when water flowing through pipes is abruptly stopped or changes direction, causing a shockwave. This can be due to quickly closing faucets, malfunctioning shut-off valves, or loose pipes allowing movement. Over time, water hammer can damage pipes and connections, leading to leaks. It's advisable to have a professional plumber assess the cause and recommend a solution, which might include installing water hammer arrestors or securing loose piping.
